source_text: Καὶ ὅτι διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ ὑμῶν καὶ διὰ τὰς εἰδωλολατρείας, ἀλλ᾿ οὐ διὰ τὸ ἐνδεὴς εἶναι τῶν τοιούτων προσφορῶν, ἐνετείλατο ὁμοίως ταῦτα γίνεσθαι, ἀκούσατε πῶς περὶ τούτων λέγει διὰ Ἀμώς, ἑνὸς τῶν δώδεκα, βοῶν· Οὐαὶ οἱ ἐπιθυμοῦντες τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ κυρίου. Ἵνα τί αὕτη ὑμῖν ἡ ἡμέρα κυρίου: Καὶ αὐτή ἐστι σκότος καὶ οὐ φῶς. Ὅν τρόπον ὅταν ἐκφύγῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ λέοντος, καὶ συναντήσῃ αὐτῷ ἡ ἄρκτος, καὶ εἰσπηδήσῃ εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπερείσηται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν τοῖχον, καὶ δάκῃ αὐτὸν ὁ ὄφις. Οὐχὶ σκότος ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου καὶ οὐ φῶς, καὶ γνόφος οὐκ ἔχων φέγγος αὐτῆς; Μεμίσηκα, ἀπῶσμαι τὰς ἑορτὰς ὑμῶν, καὶ οὐ μὴ ὀσφρανθῶ ἐν ταῖς πανηγύρεσιν ὑμῶν. Διότι ἐὰν ἐνέγκητέ μοι τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ τὰς θυσίας ὑμῶν, οὐ προσδέξομαι αὐτὰ καὶ σωτηρίου ἐπιφανείας ὑμῶν οὐκ ἐπιβλέψομαι. Ἀπόστησον ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ πλῆθος ᾠδῶν σου καὶ ψαλμῶν· ὀργάνων σου οὐκ ἀκούσομαι. Καὶ κυλισθήσεται ὡς ὕδωρ κρίμα καὶ ἡ δικαιοσύνη ὡς χειμάρρους ἄβατος. Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ; λέγει κύριος. Καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν Ῥαφάν, τοὺς τύπους, οὓς ἐποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς. Καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Δαμασκοῦ, λέγει κύριος· ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὄνομα αὐτῷ. Οὐαὶ οἱ κατασπαταλῶντες Σιὼν καὶ τοῖς πεποιθόσιν ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σαμαρείας. Οἱ ὠνομασμένοι ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀρχηγοῖς ἀπετρύγησαν ἀρχὰς ἐθνῶν· εἰσῆλθον ἑαυτοῖς οἶκος Ἰσραήλ. Διάβητε πάντες εἰς Χαλάνην καὶ ἴδετε, καὶ πορεύθητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Ἀμὰθ τὴν μεγάλην, καὶ κατάβητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Γὲθ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων, τὰς κρατίστας ἐκ πασῶν τῶν βασιλειῶν τούτων, εἰ πλείονά ἐστι τὰ ὅρια αὐτῶν τῶν ὁρίων ὑμῶν. Οἱ ἐρχόμενοι εἰς ἡμέραν πονηράν, οἱ ἐγγίζοντες καὶ ἐφαπτόμενοι σαββάτων ψευδῶν, οἱ κοιμώμενοι ἐπὶ κλινῶν ἐλεφαντίνων καὶ κατασπαταλῶντες ἐπὶ ταῖς στρωμναῖς αὐτῶν, οἱ ἐσθίοντες ἄρνας ἐκ ποιμνίων καὶ μοσχάρια ἐκ μέσου βουκολίων γαλαθηνά, οἱ ἐπικροτοῦντες πρὸς τὴν φωνὴν τῶν ὀργάνων, ὡς ἑστῶτα ἐλογίσαντο καὶ οὐχ ὡς φεύγοντα, οἱ πίνοντες ἐν φιάλαις οἶνον καὶ τὰ πρῶτα μύρα χριόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ἔπασχον οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῇ συντριβῇ τοῦ Ἰωσήφ. Διὰ τοῦτο νῦν αἰχμάλωτοι ἔσονται ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς δυναστῶν τῶν ἀποικιζομένων, καὶ μεταστραφήσεται οἴκημα κακούργων, καὶ ἐξαρθήσεται χρεμετισμὸς ἵππων ἐξ Ἐφραΐμ . Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Ἱερεμίου· Συναγάγετε τὰ κρέα ὑμῶν καὶ τὰς θυσίας καὶ φάγετε, ὅτι οὔτε περὶ θυσιῶν ἢ σπονδῶν ἐνετειλάμην τοῖς πατράσιν ὑμῶν, ῄ ἡμέρᾳ ἐπελαβόμην τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν ἐξαγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου [JÉR., VII, 21-22]. Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Δαυΐδ ἐν τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ οὕτως ἔφη· Θεὸς θεῶν κύριος ἐλάλησε, καὶ ἐκάλεσε τὴν γῆν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν ἡλίου μέχρι δυσμῶν. Ἐκ Σιὼν ἡ εὐπρέπεια τῆς ὡραιότητος αὐτοῦ. Ὁ θεὸς ἐμφανῶς ἥξει, ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, καὶ οὐ παρασιωπήσεται· πῦρ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ καυθήσεται, καὶ κύκλῳ αὐτοῦ καταιγὶς σφόδρα. Προσκαλέσεται τὸν οὐρανὸν ἂνω καὶ τὴν γῆν τοῦ διακρῖναι τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ. Συναγάγετε αὐτῷ τοὺς ὁσίους αὐτοῦ, τοὺς διατιθεμένους τὴν διαθήκην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ θυσίαις. Καὶ ἀναγγελοῦσιν οἱ οὐρανοὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, ὅτι θεὸς κριτής ἐστιν. Ἄκουσον, λαός μου, καὶ λαλήσω σοι, Ἰσραήλ, καὶ διαμαρτυροῦμαί σοι· ὁ θεός, ὁ θεός σου εἰμὶ ἐγώ. Οὐκ ἐπὶ ταῖς θυσίαις σου ἐλέγξω σε· τὰ δὲ ὁλοκαυτώματά σου ἐνώπιόν μου ἐστὶ διὰ παντός. Οὐ δέξομαι ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου σου μόσχους οὐδὲ ἐκ τῶν ποιμνίων σου χιμάρους, ὅτι ἐμά ἐστι πάντα τὰ θηρία τοῦ ἀγροῦ, κτήνη ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι καὶ βόες· ἔγνωκα πάντα τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ὡραιότης ἀγροῦ μετ᾿ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν. Ἐὰν πεινάσω, οὐ μή σοι εἴπω· ἐμὴ γάρ ἐστιν ἡ οἰκουμένη καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. Μὴ φάγωμαι κρέα ταύρων. ἢ αἷμα τράγων πίωμαι; Θῦσον τῷ θεῷ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως. καὶ ἀπόδος τῷ ὑψίστῳ τὰς εὐχάς σου· καὶ ἐπικάλεσαί με ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως, καὶ ἐξελοῦμαί σε, καὶ δοξάσεις με. Τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἵνα τί σὺ ἐκδιηγῇ τὰ δικαιώματά μου, καὶ ἀναλαμβάνεις τὴν διαθήκην μου διὰ στόματός σου; Σὺ δὲ ἐμίσησας παιδείαν καὶ ἐξέβαλες τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω. Εἰ ἐθεώρεις κλέπτην, συνέτρεχες αὐτῷ, καὶ μετὰ μοιχοῦ τὴν μερίδα σου ἐτίθεις. Τὸ στόμα σου ἐπλεόνασε κακίαν, καὶ ἡ γλῶσσά σου περιέπλεκε δολιότητας. Καθήμενος κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου κατελάλεις, καὶ κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς μητρός σου ἐτίθεις σκάνδαλον. Ταῦτα ἐποίησας, καὶ ἐσίγησα· ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος. Ἐλέγξω σε καὶ παραστήσω κατὰ πρόσωπόν σου τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου. Σύνετε δὴ ταῦτα οἱ ἐπιλανθανόμενοι τοῦ θεοῦ, μήποτε ἁρπάσῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ᾖ ὁ ῥυόμενος. Θυσία αἰνέσεως δοξάσει με, καὶ ἐκεὶ ὁδός, ἥν δείξω αὐτῷ τὸ σωτήριόν μου . Οὔτε οὖν θυσίας παρ᾿ ὑμῶν λαμβάνει, οὔτε ὡς ἐνδεὴς τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐνετείλατο ποιεῖν, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὑμῶν. Καὶ γὰρ τὸν ναὸν τὸν ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπικληθέντα οὐχ ὡς ἐνδεὴς ὢν ὡμολόγησεν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ἢ αὐλήν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅπως καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο προσέχοντες αὐτῷ μὴ εἰδωλολατρῆτε. Καὶ ὅτι τοῦτό ἐστιν, Ἡσαΐας λέγει· Ποῖον οἶκον ᾠκοδομήσατέ μοι; λέγει κύριος. Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, καὶ ἡ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου .
pass_a_gloss: And because of the sins of your people and because of the idolatries, but not because He is in need of such offerings, He commanded that these things be done. Listen to how He speaks about these things through Amos, one of the twelve, crying out: Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord. Why is this day of the Lord to you? And it is darkness and not light. Just as when a man escapes from the face of a lion, and a bear meets him, and he enters his house and leans his hands on the wall, and a snake bites him. Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light, and gloom without its shining? I have hated, I have rejected your festivals, and I will not smell in your gatherings. For if you bring me your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look at the savior of your appearances. Turn away from me the multitude of your songs and your psalms; I will not hear your instruments. And judgment will be rolled like water, and righteousness like an uncontrollable stream. Did you not bring me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness, house of Israel? says the Lord. And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the images which you made for yourselves. And I will exile you beyond Damascus, says the Lord; the God who is all-powerful is His name. Woe to those who are at ease in Zion and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria. Those who are named among the leaders have rebelled against the powers of the nations; the house of Israel has entered among them. Pass through all of them to Chalane and see, and go from there to Amath the great, and go down from there to Geth of the Philistines, the strongest of all these kingdoms, if their borders are greater than your borders. Those who come on an evil day, those who draw near and touch false sabbaths, those who sleep on ivory beds and are at ease on their couches, those who eat lambs from the flocks and calves from the midst of the herds, fat ones, those who strike the strings of instruments, thinking they are standing and not fleeing, those who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the first myrrh, and they do not suffer anything at the crushing of Joseph. Therefore, now they will be captives from the beginning of the rulers of those being exiled, and the dwelling of the wicked will be overturned, and the neighing of horses will be taken away from Ephraim. And again through Jeremiah: Gather your flesh and your sacrifices and eat, for I did not command your fathers concerning sacrifices or drink offerings on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. And again through David in the forty-eighth psalm, he said: God of gods, the Lord spoke, and He called the earth from the rising of the sun to the setting. From Zion is the beauty of His goodness. God will come openly, our God, and He will not be silent; fire will burn before Him, and a great storm will be around Him. He will call the heaven above and the earth to judge His people. Gather to Him His holy ones, those who make His covenant through sacrifices. And the heavens will declare His righteousness, for God is a judge. Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, Israel, and I will testify against you: God, your God, I am. I will not rebuke you for your sacrifices, but your whole burnt offerings are always before me. I will not accept from your house bullocks or from your flocks goats, for mine are all the animals of the field, beasts in the mountains and oxen; I know all the birds of the heaven, and the beauty of the field is with me. If I am hungry, I will not tell you; for mine is the world and its fullness. Will I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats? Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God, and pay your vows to the Most High. And call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me. But to the sinner, God said: Why do you recite my righteousness and take up my covenant with your mouth? You have hated discipline and cast my words behind you. If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you placed your portion with an adulterer. Your mouth was full of evil, and your tongue was entwined with deceit. Sitting against your brother, you spoke against him, and against the son of your mother, you placed a stumbling block. You did these things, and I was silent; you thought that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face. Understand these things, you who forget God, lest He seize, and there will be no deliverer. A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there I will show him my salvation. He does not accept sacrifices from you, nor did He command to do this because He is in need, but because of your sins. For He did not acknowledge the temple in Jerusalem, which is called by His name, as His house or His court, because He is in need, but so that you, paying attention to this, would not practice idolatry. And that this is so, Isaiah says: What house did you build for me? says the Lord. The heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet.

pass_b_english: God commanded these things to be done because of your people's sins and idolatries, not because He needs such offerings. Listen to how He speaks of these matters through Amos, one of the twelve, crying out: Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord! Why do you want this day of the Lord? It is darkness and not light. It is like a man who escapes from a lion, only to meet a bear; he enters his house and leans his hands on the wall, and a snake bites him. Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light, even gloom without any brightness? (Amos 5:18-20) I have hated and rejected your festivals, and I will not smell the offerings in your assemblies. For if you bring Me whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not accept them, nor will I look upon your peace offerings. Take away from Me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the melody of your instruments. But let justice roll down like water, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream. Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings those forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel? says the Lord. You also took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the images you made for yourselves; therefore I will exile you beyond Damascus, says the Lord, whose name is the God of Hosts. (Amos 5:25-27)

Woe to those who are at ease in Zion and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the first of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes! Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Or is their territory greater than yours? You who put far away the evil day and bring near a reign of violence; you who lie on beds of ivory and stretch out on your couches, eating lambs from the flock and fattened calves from the herd; you who sing idle songs to the sound of the harp and improvise on instruments like David; you who drink wine from bowls and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph! Therefore you shall now be the first to go into exile, the revelry of those who lounge shall pass away, and the neighing of horses shall be cut off from Ephraim. (Amos 6:1-7, 8-13)

And again through Jeremiah: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat the flesh! For I did not speak to your fathers, nor command them on the day I brought them out of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices. (Jeremiah 7:21-22) And again through David in the forty-ninth Psalm: The Mighty One, God the Lord, speaks and summons the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting. Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth. Our God comes; He does not keep silence; before Him is a devouring fire, around Him a mighty tempest. He calls to the heavens above and to the earth, that He may judge His people: Gather to Me My faithful ones, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice! The heavens declare His righteousness, for God Himself is judge! (Psalm 50:1-6)

Hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God. Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you; your burnt offerings are continually before Me. I will not accept a bull from your house or goats from your folds. For every beast of the forest is Mine, the cattle on a thousand hills. I know all the birds of the hills, and all that moves in the field is Mine. If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are Mine. Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats? Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and perform your vows to the Most High, and call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify Me. (Psalm 50:7-15)

But to the wicked God says: What right have you to recite My statutes or take My covenant on your lips? For you hate discipline, and you cast My words behind you. If you see a thief, you keep company with him, and you share with adulterers. You give your mouth free rein for evil, and your tongue frames deceit. You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your own mother's son. These things you have done, and I have been silent; you thought that I was one like yourself. But now I rebuke you and lay the charge before you. Mark this, then, you who forget God, lest I tear you apart, and there be none to deliver! The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies Me; to one who orders his way rightly I will show the salvation of God. (Psalm 50:16-23)

Therefore He does not accept sacrifices from you, nor did He command them at the beginning because He was in need, but because of your sins. For He did not acknowledge the temple in Jerusalem, which is called by His name, as His house or His court because He was in need, but so that, by paying attention to it, you might not practice idolatry. That this is so, Isaiah says: What house would you build for Me? says the Lord. Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool. (Isaiah 66:1)

review.notes: Pass B fails on scripture citation accuracy and translation fidelity regarding the Psalm number. 1. Scripture: The Greek text explicitly cites 'τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ' (the forty-ninth psalm), but Pass B cites it as 'Psalm 50:1-6'. While Psalm 49 in the Hebrew/Protestant numbering is Psalm 50 in the Septuagint, the translator must ensure the text matches the provided Greek. More critically, Pass B's citation for the Davidic passage is 'Psalm 50:1-6', but the Greek text provided is 'τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ' (49th Psalm). 2. Translation/Completeness: In the section regarding the 'crushing of Joseph', the Greek is 'συντριβῇ τοῦ Ἰωσήφ'. Pass A translates this as 'crushing of Joseph', while Pass B translates it as 'ruin of Joseph'. While 'ruin' is a valid gloss, Pass B's handling of the Amos section contains a significant addition/alteration not in the Greek: 'you who sing idle songs to the sound of the harp and improvise on instruments like David'. The Greek 'ὡς ἑστῶτα ἐλογίσαντο καὶ οὐχ ὡς φεύγοντα' refers to those who 'thought they were standing and not fleeing', which is a specific theological/descriptive point about their attitude during worship. Pass B's 'improvise on instruments like David' is an interpretive addition not present in the Greek text.
reasons: Pass B adds 'improvise on instruments like David' to the description of the people in Amos, whereas the Greek 'ὡς ἑστῶτα ἐλογίσαντο καὶ οὐχ ὡς φεύγοντα' describes their perception of their own posture (standing vs fleeing).
Pass B's scripture citation for the Davidic passage (Psalm 50) differs from the Greek's explicit 'τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ' (49th Psalm).

reasons: The Greek text is not the named work and locus. The text is from Justin Martyr's Dialogue with Trypho, but the content is not a direct quotation or reference to the work as described. The text appears to be a compilation of biblical passages and not a direct quote from Justin Martyr's work.
The translation omits significant portions of the Greek text, including the full passage from Amos, Jeremiah, and Isaiah, as well as the full psalm references.

The translation fails to preserve the negation in the phrase 'οὐ προσδέξομαι αὐτὰ' (I will not accept them), which is translated as 'I will not accept them' but the original Greek clearly denies the acceptance.

The translation fails to preserve the agency in the phrase 'ἐνετείλατο ὁμοίως ταῦτα γίνεσθαι' (He commanded these things to be done), which is translated as 'He commanded these things to be done' but the original Greek clearly attributes the command to God.

The translation fails to preserve the modality in the phrase 'ἐνετείλατο ὁμοίως ταῦτα γίνεσθαι' (He commanded these things to be done), which is translated as 'He commanded these things to be done' but the original Greek clearly indicates a command.

The translation fails to preserve the doctrine in the phrase 'ὁ θεὸς ἐμφανῶς ἥξει' (God will come openly), which is translated as 'God will come openly' but the original Greek clearly indicates a future event.

The translation fails to match the inline citations to the actual words quoted or alluded to, including verse numbering. For example, the citation for Amos 5:18-20 is incorrect and does not match the actual text.
